name: Andorra

findings.summary: Andorra Telecom chose Huawei as sole vendor to swap its nationwide FTTH network from EPON to GPON, using Huawei MA5800 OLTs, ONTs and home Wi-Fi routers, with rollout scheduled March 2017 to about January 2018.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc under the equipment-vendor rule (Huawei supplies OLT firmware). Tier 3 as a sole-vendor award with named counterparty but no value. Not corroborated: the Broadband Communities piece appears to rewrite the same Huawei release, so the sources are not independent. Pre-2020; whether Huawei OLTs remain in service (Andorra Telecom later advertised 10 Gbps fibre) was not confirmed.

findings.controller: Google Cloud, Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Oracle (plus T-Systems)
findings.summary: Andorra Digital launched a sovereign-cloud framework giving public and private bodies access to Google Cloud, AWS, Microsoft, T-Systems and Oracle at nationally negotiated rates, requiring European data residency and client-held encryption keys; no cost figures were disclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole us because four of five listed providers are US hyperscalers; T-Systems (German) is a third-pole option within the same framework. Tier 2 as a negotiated framework with no individual contracts reported. Not corroborated: both sources are the same S3 outlet and no S1/S2 source was opened. 'Sovereign key' is the government's claim; hosting is in Europe, not Andorra.

findings.summary: Andorra's government, through Andorra Digital, signed a strategic agreement with Google Cloud to speed public- and private-sector digital transformation, including sovereign-cloud services and AI; no value, instrument type or hosting location was given.
findings.analyst_inference: Coded Tier 1 because the source calls it a strategic agreement without binding terms or value; it appears to be the precursor to the 2026 multi-provider framework (AND-002). No AI model named, so no models finding.

findings.summary: Andorra Telecom, the national operator, runs three own data centres (La Massana, La Comella, Nexus) and received a CEEDA Operations energy-efficiency plaque for them at DCD Connect Madrid in May 2025; capacity not stated.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic: Andorra Telecom is understood to be state-owned (analyst inference, not stated in the source). Tier 5 because the award recognises the sites' current operations, hence still_current true as of May 2025. Not an AI campus; general-purpose telco/hosting facilities of unknown MW.

silicon.null_reason: no accelerator purchases or deployments surfaced in data-centre and AI-partnership searches; none expected at this scale

models.null_reason: an April 2026 report says the government plans a Copilot-like AI tool for public workers by 2027, but names no vendor or model provider

applications.null_reason: no safe-city or surveillance vendor found; an Encamp council AI platform surfaced only as a headline and was not opened

power.null_reason: no AI- or data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced in other searches

research_gaps: Which vendor supplies Andorra Telecom's 5G RAN and core (44 sites, 3.5 GHz, 91% coverage by Dec 2025)? No search named Ericsson, Nokia, Huawei or ZTE.
Are Huawei OLTs from the 2017 FTTH swap still in service after the later 10 Gbps fibre upgrade, and who supplied that upgrade?
Which vendor or model provider will power the planned 2027 public-administration AI tool (reporting hints at Microsoft)?
What is the Encamp council AI platform (Dec 2025) and on whose stack is it built?
Which individual contracts have been signed under the Andorra Digital sovereign-cloud framework, and with which providers?
